5. Deviations from spec
- Opt-in. The default inspectSessionOwnerRuntime still answers 'unavailable' off Linux; only a caller passing probableLiveness: true gets status 'live' with probable: true (or 'reused' after a reboot). Reason: test :819 pins 'unavailable' off Linux and the DoD says nothing else changes, so a default flip would turn it red natively. It also keeps retirement and orphan-archive decisions off a probable status.
- Storage: the boot minute (now minus os.uptime, floored to the minute, Ruling 111) is stored in the existing processStartId slot, so descriptor validation and fixtures are unchanged. Adjacent minutes (tolerance 1, as the audit-lock owner) count as the same boot. On win32 a runtime is recorded only if the pid exists at registration (mirrors Linux null).
- 'Says probably': the warning is a structured object with no prose. Added probable: true plus a message containing 'probably live', only in the probable case; the Linux warning keeps its exact four keys.
- Per-commit record checkpoint skipped; one terminal write, as briefed. resultSha256 is the string 'not-computed': once the cap was reached guard-dispatch-budget admitted only record writes, git add and git commit, so the finalizer (scratch/csw-f-finalize.mjs, prepare mode tested, finalize mode untested) could not run. Re-bind as sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of this text.

6. Open items
- Behaviour shift (Linux parity, not a defect): a win32 descriptor registered after this commit whose owner pid is later dead now reads 'not-live' by default (was 'unavailable'), so retirement reads 'retirable' and the orphan-archive tier refuses it as observable.
- Un-skipping the first MULTISESSION test on win32 would see extra probable/message keys at its deepEqual (:1918); the owning test slice must expect them.
- Unverified: whether os.uptime() on Windows counts sleep. If it does not, the boot minute drifts after each sleep and a live session reads 'reused' (a quiet miss).
- No test exercises the hermetic win32 seams on a non-win32 host (tests forbidden here). Follow-up test slice: platform/nowMs/uptimeSeconds seams on Linux; boot mismatch gives 'reused'; ESRCH gives 'not-live'; the +-1 minute edge; opt-in versus default.
